anti-aligned spins. This specific ratio is significant as it provides insights into the

Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) frequency is significant because it directly relates to
the nuclear spin properties of isotopes, which influence how they interact with an
external magnetic field. The frequency at which a nucleus resonates is determined by its
magnetic moment and the strength of the magnetic field applied. For example, 17 O has a
nuclear spin of 5/2 and a specific gyromagnetic ratio that results in a resonance
frequency of 115.5 MHz when subjected to a 20.0 T magnetic field. This frequency is
calculated using the Larmor equation, which links the magnetic field strength to the
precession frequency of the nuclear spins, thus highlighting the unique properties of 17 O
in NMR studies. Understanding these frequencies is crucial for interpreting NMR spectra
and gaining insights into molecular structures and dynamics.
answers.explanation: correct because it accurately describes how the NMR frequency is influenced by the nuclear spin properties and gyromagnetic ratio of 17O in relation to the strength of the applied magnetic field, resulting in a specific resonance frequency of 115.5 MHz at 20.0 T.
